Oct 27 (Reuters) - Nvidia [(NVDA.O), opens new tab](https://www.reuters.com/markets/companies/NVDA.O) and Meta [(META.O), opens new tab](https://www.reuters.com/markets/companies/META.O) said on Tuesday they would deepen their partnership ​on the Muse AI assistant and ‌related AI models, with Nvidia investing $3 billion in the Facebook parent's equity offering.

Here are some details:

Learn about the latest breakthroughs in AI and tech with the Reuters Artificial Intelligencer newsletter. Sign up [here.](/newsletters/reuters-ai/?location=article-paragraph&redirectUrl=%2Ftechnology%2Fnvidia-meta-partner-muse-agent-nvidia-invests-3-billion-2026-10-27%2F)

-   Meta's ​Muse models and agents, which run ​on Nvidia infrastructure, will work more closely ⁠with the chipmaker to improve performance ​and reduce costs

-   Muse, known internally as Hatch, ​is central to CEO Mark Zuckerberg's plan to deliver "personal superintelligence" to the billions of people who use ​Meta's services daily

-   Modeled on the open-source AI ​agent OpenClaw, Muse can access a user's email, calendar, ‌payments, ⁠health, shopping and smart-home applications, with users able to revoke access at any time

-   Earlier in the day, Meta [increased](https://www.reuters.com/legal/transactional/meta-launches-35-billion-stock-offering-fund-ai-expansion-2026-10-26/) its equity offering ​to $97.5 billion, ​the largest ⁠fundraising in its history, as it accelerates investment in AI ​infrastructure

-   The companies may also explore working ​together ⁠more on Nvidia's OpenShell framework, including using it to roll out software safely and using ⁠a ​tool called Sentry to ​monitor how AI agents behave


Reporting by Shivani Tanna in ​Bengaluru; Editing by Sonia Cheema and Sherry Jacob-Phillips
